THE 30-SECOND VERSION

What happens to a promise after the meeting ends?

Automate the context. Let people confirm the accountability.

23survey responses
6depth interviews
2product capabilities

Independent capstone · prototype. Research scope and measurement limits are explained below.

01 / PROBLEM

The summary is finished. The work isn’t.

An action item can be captured correctly and still go nowhere. Ownership changes, priorities shift, and the meeting record stops reflecting reality. I explored this gap between recording a commitment and reaching an explicit outcome.

02 / CONTRIBUTION

What I worked on

I brought the research, problem framing, solution prioritization, prototype, adoption strategy and measurement plan into one capstone. The product proposal centres on two capabilities: Commitment Checkpoint and Commitment Pulse.

03 / EVIDENCE

What changed my understanding

The research combined 23 survey responses, six depth interviews and two WhatsApp follow-ups. It pointed beyond forgetting: unclear ownership, competing priorities and ambiguous definitions of done also mattered. This is directional research, not a representative estimate of the entire market.

04 / DECISION

Two focused bets

Checkpoint lets a person accept, correct, reassign or decline AI-suggested ownership. Pulse resurfaces the commitment before the next relevant moment, so its state can be updated. I kept the solution attached to existing meeting behaviour instead of adding another daily task inbox.

05 / SOLUTION

A commitment has a lifecycle

The proposed flow moves from capture to human confirmation, then contextual follow-up and an explicit outcome: done, reassigned or deliberately dropped. The prototype makes those decisions visible and preserves the meeting context behind them.

06 / TRADEOFFS

Trust before automation breadth

Wrong ownership would undermine the entire experience. The proposal preserves human confirmation, limits notification frequency and keeps analytics at the commitment level. Sprint planning, workload scoring and autonomous closure stay outside the scope.

07 / MEASUREMENT

How I would know it works

The capstone proposes a six-month target of increasing 14-day honest commitment resolution from a case-study baseline of 28% to 45%. This is a target, not a delivered uplift. A pilot would compare the existing action-item flow with Checkpoint plus Pulse, while tracking false ownership, dismissals and notification fatigue.

08 / LEARNING

The next proof is behavioural

A working interaction is only the first step. The next test is whether recurring customer-facing teams keep using the loop and close commitments more reliably without performing superficial status updates.
